title: Merge Hell
cards: Agentic coding made us faster.
A whole week's code before breakfast.
Forty pull requests. I tagged the team.
The lead said: We need time to review them properly.
Of course! Quality comes first.
So while they reviewed them...
I made ten more.
Ten more!
And they were doing good reviews!
Checking edge cases. Finding real bugs.
One guy spent two hours understanding a race condition.
During those two hours, I created three new services.
He was still on the first service!
Then they organized a review day.
No coding. Everyone clears the backlog.
Everyone except my agents.
By lunch they'd reviewed fifty.
The queue had grown by ninety.
And they said: We're making good progress.
Good progress!
They asked me to help.
I built a dashboard to track the backlog.
Then I tagged them to review it.
They asked for smaller pull requests.
Very reasonable. Easier to understand.
So I split the next one into three.
Three pull requests! Three reviews!
Three pipelines!
The lead said: This is like Sisyphus.
I said: No, he had one rock.
Our rocks create more rocks.
At five they said: We'll finish tomorrow.
Tomorrow!
I left the agents running overnight.
They'll be reviewing until Tomorrowland.
Management asked if we'd saved time.
I said: I've saved loads.
Their time? I've booked the next six years.
